To find the physical dimension of the constant $k$, we start with the given relationship:
$\text{Force} = k \times \text{Length}$

For the equation to be dimensionally consistent, the dimensions on both sides must be equal:
$[\text{Force}] = [k] \times [\text{Length}]$

The physical dimension of Force is derived from Newton's Second Law ($F = ma$):
- Mass has the dimension $\text{Mass}$.
- Acceleration is the change in velocity over time, and velocity is length over time. Thus, acceleration has the dimension $\frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2}$.
Therefore, $[\text{Force}] = \text{Mass} \times \frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2}$

Substituting this into the dimensional equation:
$\text{Mass} \times \frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2} = [k] \times \text{Length}$

To solve for $[k]$, we divide both sides by $\text{Length}$:
$[k] = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2 \times \text{Length}}$
$[k] = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Time}^2}$

<ANSWER>Mass / Time^2</ANSWER>
